meta.title: The E Form: One String Makes It Major
meta.summary: Five of the E form's six strings are a root or a fifth, so the whole quality of the most-used chord on the guitar rests on a single note.

Five of the six strings are root or fifth. That leaves exactly one string carrying the note that actually decides what chord this is:

The workhorse chord of the instrument hangs on a single string.

It's also one of only two forms in this chapter you play exactly as written, barre and all, instead of in pieces — the other being the A form. Every one of those six notes rings; no fragment habit needed here.

, the power chord with a low-E root. It's the same shape the A form gave you on strings 5-4-3; the two full-barre forms in this chapter each hide one, which is a large part of why both feel like home.

This is also why the E form stays the shape you navigate the rest of the neck from.
